scenes.title: Identify the built-in Training record form

captions.text: In Records, the New Record form has Training selected in Definition.
This built-in form provides course information, a narrative, participant
rows and optional unit times.
Our fictional Chicago Fire exercise demonstrates the record lifecycle.
It does not represent a physical training session or attendance.
Enter a distinct Course, Training Only, Records Software Entry,
followed by the exercise date.
The Course code is Academy Rec Twenty-Nine, and External ID carries
a separate exercise reference.
Location says Fictional Software Workspace.
Review Start and the empty End before continuing.

captions.text: Chicago Fire can use this pattern for a software orientation record.
Community care and mental-health teams can document an operational software
exercise without client histories.
Search-and-rescue teams can keep practice documentation
distinct from a mission response.
Security teams can retain a fictional platform exercise; wildland
coordinators can document seasonal software familiarization; industrial
teams can preserve a system-training example and public handout.
Across all six settings, use accurate narrative, actual participants and times
only when they occurred, a verified attachment, and the saved revision that
supports the statement being reviewed.
